conventions.convention: Registers Q_d have positive dimension d; the zero-qubit register is the one-dimensional empty tensor product C, distinct from C^0.
The root inner product is linear in its first argument and conjugate-linear in its second; tensor pairings multiply the factor pairings.
Factor order is retained, product bases are lexicographic, and bit position 0 is most significant: enc_n(x) = sum over k<n of x_k 2^(n-1-k). The empty word has index 0.
General tensor spaces allow zero-dimensional factors, which make the tensor space zero. The empty factor list instead gives C. P_sigma outputs the factors in order sigma(0), ..., sigma(n-1).
Partial trace contracts the second factor: its (i,i') entry is the sum over j of R_((i,j),(i',j)). Rows are outputs and columns inputs; an empty contracted index gives zero.
The tensor map for an empty family is the identity on C.

load_bearing.statement: Ordered tensor spaces retain factor order, use lexicographic product bases and the product inner product, take the empty tensor product to be C, allow zero-dimensional factors, and define wire permutations by their action on product bases.

Elementary tensors of the specified ordered orthonormal factor bases form an orthonormal basis, and tensor dimensions multiply; the empty list has dimension 1 and any zero-dimensional factor gives the zero space.

For finite ordered families of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces and linear maps, the tensor map is the unique linear map applying the factor maps to elementary tensors; the empty tensor map is the identity on C.
Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space. If D:V→V is linear and tr(D∘A)=0 for every linear map A:V→V, then D=0. This includes the zero space.

For finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces H_A,H_B, partial trace is the unique linear map satisfying tr((Tr_B R)∘T)=tr(R∘(T⊗I_B)) for every R and T of the stated endomorphism spaces. Its coordinate formula is independent of the chosen ordered orthonormal basis of H_B, including zero-dimensional factors.

For integer d≥1, Q_d=C^d has the standard first-linear inner product and ordered standard computational basis. An n-qubit register is the ordered tensor product of n copies of Q_2, with empty product C.

alerts.finding: lem-qa-tensor-extension-preserves-operator-norm, Proof 3.1, says: “P and P^{-1} preserve norms, so each has operator norm 1.” Its separate conjugation clause permits a finite ordered tensor register with a zero-dimensional factor under def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation. On that zero space, P and P^{-1} have operator norm 0 by the opened published def-operator-norm-on-a-finite-dimensional-inner-product-space. The stated conjugation equality remains true, but this proof assertion omits that boundary case.
